Thanks Logan — I reviewed the redline. Below are my counsel notes and a recommended approach for a controlled counter. I attached a PDF with inline comments for their exact redline locations (Redwood_DPA_comments_R1.pdf).

Key positions (summary):
- Transfers: We accept SCCs. Recommend we offer SCCs + Redwood transfer schedule (short addendum) to reduce back-and-forth; we should not agree to open-ended transfer mechanisms.
- Subprocessors: Provide current named list and commit to notice + right to object only for material subprocessors (clear threshold: direct access to raw customer data / decrypting access). We should avoid an approval right for every minor change.
- Liability / Indemnity: We should not accept unlimited liability for security events. Recommended cap: greater of 12 months of fees or $1,500,000 for this account (if they push on lower, propose fee-based metric). For willful misconduct / gross negligence carveouts, keep defined narrow exceptions.
- Retention & Deletion: We can accept specific data retention periods for customer data and standard post-termination deletion/return language. For backups, we propose a 90-day retention window for data restoration; after that data is irrecoverable.
- Security Evidence: Provide SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 summaries via secure Drive link. Full artifacts available under NDA if they require.
- Subprocessor sub-clauses: Accept notification + 30 days to object for material subprocessors, otherwise deemed accepted.
- Execution: DocuSign is fine. For contract control, propose Redwood signs via DocuSign and requests NimHealth to counter-sign within 14 days, otherwise contract moves to next steps per procurement.

Next steps (recommended):
1) I will prepare a focused counter (Redwood_DPA_counter_R1.docx) preserving our limits and offering SCCs + a transfer schedule.
2) Laura to post subprocessor CSV and SOC2 summary to the Drive folder.
3) Priyom to confirm commercial process/PO timing.

I will mark the items that are negotiable in the draft; anything highlighted as "must have" is where I need you to confirm business risk appetite.

-Neha

Nicole / Arun — thanks for sending the redline and for the clarity on timing. Apologies for the short pause while we coordinated internally. Below is Redwood's position and next steps.

Short summary of Redwood positions: 
- Transfers: We will accept the EU/UK SCCs. Neha will attach a short transfer schedule/addendum that maps the SCCs to our service model (see Drive link).
- Subprocessors: We will provide a named subprocessor list (shared to Drive). Redwood agrees to notice of new material subprocessors with a 30-day objection window; we cannot provide pre-approval for routine operational suppliers.
- Liability: We cannot accept an open-ended unlimited liability clause. For NimHealth we propose a cap of liability equal to the greater of 12 months of paid Redwood fees under the agreement or USD 1,500,000. We are willing to discuss limited carveouts for gross negligence/willful misconduct.
- Retention: Redwood will accept the proposed retention/deletion framework with the standard 90-day backups window.

Attached is our focused counter-redline (Redwood_DPA_counter_R1.docx). I also uploaded SOC2 summary and the current subprocessor CSV to the shared Drive folder. If we can get alignment on liability cap and SCCs, we can move to DocuSign.

Please review and let me know if you prefer a brief call tomorrow to walk through the two open items (liability cap + subprocessor objection mechanics). Otherwise we'll place the counter into DocuSign for signature: https://docusign.net/envelope/ABC123nimhealth.

Priyom — procurement / finance notes? If they want a PO-first flow we'll accommodate, but e-signature will speed execution for our side.

Thanks all — looking forward to wrapping this up.

Best,
